name: Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, National Marine Conservation Area Reserve, and Haida Heritage Site
blurb: Salmon, bears and seabirds linking Haida rainforest to the sea.

tip.title: Remove the salmon
tip.text: Salmon feed bears, eagles, sea lions and orcas, and their carcasses feed ravens and the forest. Set Pacific salmon to -100% and watch the predators on land and at sea.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve and Haida Heritage Site

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light drives the growth of rainforest trees on land and of kelp and plankton in the sea.
Break down fallen trees, salmon carcasses and dead marine life, returning nutrients to soil and water.
A large conifer of the coastal rainforest. Bald eagles nest in big coastal trees like it.

nodes.name: Western red cedar
nodes.desc: Dominant rainforest conifer in Gwaii Haanas. Browsed by introduced deer, which can limit young cedars.
Evergreen shrub of the forest understory with berries; understory plants like it are browsed by deer.
Canopy kelp that forms forests in cool coastal water. Parks Canada and Haida partners work on kelp restoration here.
Drifting microscopic algae that feed zooplankton and krill. General ecological knowledge.

nodes.name: Sitka black-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Introduced to Haida Gwaii, now abundant, and browses native plants heavily. With no wolves on the islands, bears and hunters are the main predators.

nodes.name: Krill and zooplankton
nodes.desc: Small drifting crustaceans that eat phytoplankton and feed fish, seabirds and whales.
Schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is prey for sea lions, whales and eagles.
Spawn in the more than 100 salmon streams of Gwaii Haanas, carrying ocean nutrients into the forest.
Introduced by ships. Rats eat seabird eggs and chicks, and have devastated murrelet colonies. Eradication has been carried out on some Gwaii Haanas islands.
Clever scavenger that feeds on carcasses such as spawned-out salmon and deer.
Large eared seal that eats fish such as herring and salmon, and is prey for orcas.
Feeds in the waters around Gwaii Haanas on krill and small schooling fish, which makes the area a key feeding habitat.
Nests in coastal trees. Takes fish and seabirds, and scavenges.
Top marine predator. Mammal-eating orcas hunt sea lions and whales; other orcas eat fish like salmon.
